# Stock and materials

The studio holds two kinds of stock: raw materials such as clay and glaze, and finished pieces waiting to be sold. Both are tracked in the same spreadsheet but counted differently.

## Clay and glazes

Clay arrives in twenty-kilo bags from a supplier in the next county. We reorder when fewer than fifteen bags remain on the shelf, since deliveries can take a fortnight. Glazes are mixed in small batches and labelled with the recipe and date. Any batch older than six months is tested on a tile before being used on real work, because some colours shift as they age.

## Finished goods

Finished pieces are counted every Friday afternoon. Seconds, meaning pieces with small flaws, are stored on a separate rack and sold at the spring market. Each shelf is labelled by collection so that anyone can find a teapot or a set of bowls without opening the spreadsheet.

## Kiln supplies

Kiln shelves, posts and cones wear out over time. Elena checks them after every firing and writes cracked shelves on the whiteboard in the workshop. Replacement shelves are expensive, so we order them in pairs twice a year rather than one at a time. Cones are bought in boxes of fifty from the same supplier as the clay.
